questions.stem: Code calls Employee result = em2.merge(emp), then emp.setSalary(200000) and commits. What happens to that salary?

options.text: It is written, because merge() attached emp itself to em2.
options.says: merge() does not attach its argument: it copies the argument's state into a managed instance and returns that instance.

options.text: It is lost, because em2 tracks the instance merge() returned, not emp.
options.says: The argument stays detached, so dirty checking never sees changes made to it after the merge; only changes to the returned copy are flushed.

options.text: The commit fails, because emp was changed while a transaction was open.
options.says: Changing a detached object is allowed and raises nothing; the change simply is not tracked by any persistence context.

questions.stem: Why does the page use a record as a DTO projection rather than as a JPA entity?

options.text: JPA needs a no-arg constructor and non-final fields, which a record does not have.
options.says: A record's fields are final and its only constructor takes every component, so the provider cannot build it empty and fill it.

options.text: A record cannot carry annotations on its components, so JPA cannot map its columns.
options.says: Record components can be annotated; the obstacle is the fixed, final state, not the annotations.

options.text: A record cannot be named in a JPQL query, so JPA could never load one.
options.says: The page's own JPQL builds a record with SELECT new ..., so records do appear in queries, as projections.
